description:
Found by the #423 probes (s424), PRE-EXISTING (identical before and after that
fix -- both sides read `object-address` of the typeglob struct).

    my $r1 = \*main::foo; my $r2 = \*main::foo;
    print +($r1 == $r2 ? "same" : "diff"), "|", ("$r1" eq "$r2" ? "eqstr" : "nestr");

    perl : same|eqstr
    PCL  : diff|nestr

CAUSE: `p-make-typeglob` does `(make-p-typeglob pkg name)` -- a FRESH struct on
every evaluation -- so the referent identity that #163 made stable for scalars,
arrays and hashes is not stable for globs.  `*main::foo` names a slot in the
symbol table; two mentions must denote ONE object, exactly as `\$x == \$x`
holds because $x has one box.

This is the same defect #163 fixed one level up (a fresh WRAPPER per `\`); here
it is a fresh REFERENT per mention, which no wrapper rule can repair.

FIX SHAPE: intern typeglobs per (package, name) in a weak-valued table --
`p-make-typeglob` returns the existing struct when there is one.  Then
`object-address` is stable, `==` is true, the two strings agree, and a glob
stored in two places stays one object (which is also what a future
`*foo{ARRAY}`-style slot model needs).
CHECK: `p-glob-copy` and the *p-filehandles* registry key on (package, name)
strings today, so interning should be invisible to them -- verify.
BAR: probes (== , "" , refaddr, a glob ref through a container, a blessed glob
ref) + the full sweep; op/ + io/ companion legs (glob identity shows up in
op/gv.t and the IO files).
title: Two \*main::foo are NOT the same reference: p-make-typeglob mints a fresh struct per evaluation, so == is false and the two print different addresses (#163 family)
